title: Simplify batcher statechart and introduce KV-cache contracts for restartable shards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: The continuous-batching codepath and KV cache lifecycle have accreted ad-hoc transitions, making graceful restart, shard handoff, and eviction semantics brittle. This ticket aims to replace the tangled state machine with a small, explicit statechart and to formalize a KV-cache contract so shards can be restarted or migrated safely without long tail latencies or stale-kv anomalies. Scope: refactor in-memory batcher state transitions, implement per-shard KV cache contract (checkpoint/epoch/owned flag), add idempotent restart hooks, and remove two legacy timers used for emergency eviction. Non-goals: full re-architecture of prefetch logic, changing admission control heuristics (will follow in a separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Batcher transitions codified into a statechart with <=6 states and deterministic transitions documented in DESIGN doc
KV cache exposes a minimal contract: checkpoint(), restore(epoch), mark_owned(), snapshot_cleanup() and all shards honor contract
Canary rollout reduces 95th percentile tail latency for continuous small requests (<=64 tokens) by >=20% on canary cluster
No increase in memory usage >5% at peak compared to baseline; integration e2e tests for restartable shards pass
Feature flag 'batch_statechart_v2' exists and allows safe rollback without process restart
design_notes: Rationale: current state spread across batcher.go, prefetch_manager.go and kvcache.go. Consolidate transition rules in a single lightweight statechart implementation to simplify reasoning and testing.
Statechart: IDLE -> PREFETCHING -> READY -> IN_FLIGHT -> DRAINING -> QUIESCED; transitions include epoch checks and lease tokens.
KV contract: every shard maintains epoch metadata (monotonic), last_checkpoint_ptr, and an ownership bit. Checkpoint/restore operations must be atomic w.r.t. new writes.
Restart semantics: when a shard restarts, it must call restore(epoch) and refuse IN_FLIGHT transitions until snapshot validation completes. This prevents stale KV reads during handoff.
Dependency change: bump async-runtime crate from 0.9.x to 1.2.x (must audit task::spawn compat and timer APIs). We'll keep adapter layer to limit surface area.
Trade-offs: introducing explicit checkpointing adds a small stall during shard restore; mitigated by asynchronous background warming and a short prefetch grace window.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (3d): Add statechart module, wire a shadow implementation that logs transitions without changing behavior. Unit tests for legal/illegal transitions.
Phase 2 (4d): Implement KV contract APIs and shim kvcache to call checkpoint/restore paths. Add epoch tag to each cache entry header.
Phase 3 (5d): Wire statechart into live batcher code under feature flag 'batch_statechart_v2' and add per-shard restart hooks. Introduce a short snapshot validation step during restore.
Phase 4 (2d): Remove legacy emergency timers behind flag after 48h of canary stability. Clean up old transitional code.
Phase 5 (2d): Run load test matrix and rollout to canary Dedicated pool, collect metrics, and follow rollback/rollforward decision tree.
Implementation notes: keep PRs small and reviewable: one PR per phase. Mark with codeowners: @serving-runtime and @kvcache-maintainers.
rollout_plan: Deploy binary with flag present to staging and run end-to-end test harness (local + stress)
Enable flag for 5% of canary Dedicated instances for 6 hours; monitor 95th tail, error rate, and kvcache eviction counts
If stable, increase to 25% for 24 hours and run long-lived stability tests (24h), then 100% of canary pool
Schedule Dedicated production rollout during low-traffic window with a 2-hour observability hold and immediate rollback path
Rollback: flip flag off -> wait for in-flight to drain -> revert to baseline behavior. Keep old code paths in place for one release cycle before deleting.
test_plan: Unit tests: statechart transitions, illegal transition assertions, kvcache contract invariants
Integration tests: shard restart simulation with concurrent writes and reads, verify no stale reads or missing entries
Load tests: synthetic continuous small requests (8-64 tokens) at 10k qps on canary; compare latency percentiles vs baseline
Chaos tests: simulate OOM GC and process restart to validate snapshot/restore durability
Perf regression suite: ensure token throughput and CPU/GC are within ±5% of baseline or improved
monitoring_and_metrics: 95p and 99p tail latency for continous-batching route (metric: serving.latency.continuous.tok_64.p99)
Checkpoint duration and restore duration histograms (serving.kvcache.checkpoint.ms)
Feature flag rollout gauge and active shards using v2 (serving.feature.batch_statechart_v2.gauge)
Error rates and stale-read counter (serving.kvcache.stale_reads.count) must be zero in production after rollout
blockers: Async runtime bump has an ABI surface that breaks an internal timer adapter used by prefetch; need a minor adapter shim (owner: infra-lib)
Need sign-off from platform-security on checkpoint metadata exposure (ticket SEC-1122) before broad rollout
Two failing flaky integration tests on staging (investigating race in restore validation)
